symptom: In synthetic Node 22.16.0, overriding RegExp.prototype.test to return false could hide embedded synthetic path tokens and reject valid date fields, while returning true could admit a malformed contextDigest after re-digesting. Capturing the native test function alone was insufficient: its RegExpExec dispatch still consulted mutable RegExp.prototype.exec, permitting selective path-token suppression or malformed hex admission. No actual private paths, K archive, odds, database or production evidence was used.
lesson: A content digest does not authenticate semantic admission if a caller can modify ambient RegExp.prototype.test or exec. Capturing test alone does not isolate regex matching because built-in test delegates to mutable exec. Verify the complete dispatch chain, not just the named method.
guardrail: For fixed non-global shadow-evidence patterns, invoke a module-captured native RegExp.prototype.exec directly through Reflect.apply and compare with null; do not call mutable .test or delegate to prototype .exec. Regression-test both reversible ambient hooks, valid evidence compatibility, embedded synthetic path rejection and malformed digest rejection. Keep all artifacts research-only and productionConnection=false.
